title: Morrow: company memory that AI agents can rely on
excerpt: Morrow gives AI agents company memory they can rely on. It pulls Slack, Linear, GitHub, Notion, calls and tickets into one reviewed layer, turns it into skill files an agent can run, and serves it through an API. Every answer names the evidence it came from. webvise designed and built Morrow in-house, without a client.
challenge: A company's decisions are scattered across Slack threads, calls, tickets, docs and pull requests. Search returns fragments, and docs drift from how the team works. Agents then either keep asking people or answer from sources that contradict each other. Morrow asks how agents can get memory that someone has reviewed and keeps current, so that nobody has to check every response.
solution: Morrow has two screens. The landing page explains the problem and the workflow behind the product: ingest, resolve, approve, publish and learn. The operator dashboard shows the health of the memory, the state of each source connector and a queue of contradictions. Each conflict is resolved with its evidence and waits for a person to approve it. The dashboard also holds the generated skill files and an audit trail. Sources that contradict each other become review tasks, and nothing reaches an agent until an owner signs off. Approved context goes to agents through guarded API endpoints, which serve reviewed memory and skill files and never the open queue. The interface looks like a lab instrument, with an animated graph of the context, and is built in Next.js 16.
